9. It appears from sub-section (3) of the above quoted section 3 that the provisions under BCIL Act, 1997 have been given over-riding effect over the provisions of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 and the Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972 by providing that the provisions of the said two legislations will be applicable subject to the provisions of the BCIL Act, 1997 (এই আইনের বিধান সাপেক্ষে). Section 4 provided as to who would be the sponsors of the Bank. Section 5 provided, amongst others, that the authorized capital of the Bank would be Taka 200 crore and the paid up capital would be Taka 92 crore. Sub-section (2) of section 5 divided the share-holding of the said shares into three categories, namely 'Ka' Class, 'Kha' Class and 'Ga' Class share holders, and made provisions for allotment of shares among them out of the said paid-up capital of Taka 92 crore, thereby pro-viding that 'Ka' Class share-holders would contribute to the paid-up capital for an amount of Taka 20 crore, 'Kha' Class shareholders for an amount of Taka 20 crore and 'Ga' Class share-holders for an amount of Taka 52 crore etc. Sections 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 dealt with some other aspects of the BCBL, namely the procedures of payment of share money, formation of the Board of Directors etc., and section 11 elaborated the processes as to how the liabilities of the Bank towards its depositors would be adjusted. Sub-section (3) of section 16 of the said Act provided that the provisions of Limitation Act, 1908 would not be applicable to the said Bank in respect of realization of liability towards the said Bank, thereby confirming the special and distinct nature of the said legislation. Section 19, however, provided for the power of Bangladesh Bank to issue directions in consultation with the government in respect of matters which were not included in the BCIL Act, 1997, though they were required to be included therein, and such, directions to be issued by the Bangladesh Bank would be regarded as the provisions of the BCIL Act, 1997. Apart from above provisions, section 20 of the said Act has given a power on the government to clear any ambiguity in the implementation of the provisions of the said Act by issuing orders within five years after establishment of the said Bank. However, sub-section (2) of section 20 provided that such orders of the government had to be placed before the Parliament as early as possible. 

 10. Upon analyzing the entire text of the BCIL Act, 1997, it appears that the said Act was enacted by the Parliament for some particular purposes as mentioned in the preamble of the said Act, and some limitations of power of the Bank, its shareholders, Bangladesh Bank and the government, to be exercised in respect of the said Bank, have been mentioned. There is no doubt that the BCIL Act, 1997 is a special law enacted for special purpose. It has been given rather special over-riding status by providing the words “এই আইনের বিধান সাপেক্ষে” ("subject to the provision of this Act") as incorporated under sub-section (3) of section 3, thereby out-playing the effects of the provisions under the Bank Companies Act, 1991 and the Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972, two other special legislations. Therefore, this BCIL Act, 1997 has been enacted for establishment of a special bank and almost all vital matters have been mentioned in the said Act for the purpose of such establishment and running of the business of the said bank. Though the Government has been given some supervisory powers under several provisions of the BCBL Act, 1997 to intervene, sub-section (2) of section 20 restricts such power by providing that if any order is issued by it during a period of first five (5) years, that order has to be placed before the Parliament as early as possible. This sub-section (2) of section 20 expresses in clear terms the anxiety of our Legislature in establishing the BCBL.
